drills.name: 1 Reload 1
drills.notes: 7 yards onto an IPSC/USPSA silhouette. Load a single round, chamber it, and holster with a full spare magazine ready. On the beep, draw and fire 1 round, take the slide-lock reload, then fire 1 more — isolates the exact moment the gun runs dry so the reload gets full attention, not the shooting. No official pass/fail; commonly cited par across trainers runs roughly 2.5–4 seconds, with 3.5s a solid working target. Load a magazine with just 1 round to start, then reload with a full (or spare) magazine for the second shot.

stages.name: Draw, 1, Reload, 1
stages.notes: Draw and fire 1 round, take the slide-lock reload, then fire 1 more. That's 1 round before the reload — load a magazine with just 1 in it, then reload with a fresh (or full) magazine for the second shot.

drills.name: 26-Round Fundamentals Check
drills.notes: 7 yards, two USPSA/IPSC targets, all from concealment. A-zone body or full head box counts as 5 points, so 130 points are available across 26 rounds. Covers draws, grip and recovery, transitions and reloads — scale it by setting yourself a hit factor goal. The three one-shot draws are separate stages so each is timed on its own. The Slide-Lock Reload stage starts with just 3 rounds loaded so the mag runs dry on cue — reload with a full (or another 3-round) magazine to finish.

stages.name: Bill Drill
stages.notes: Draw and fire 6 rounds to the A-zone on one target.

stages.name: One-Shot Draw 3
stages.notes: Draw and fire 1 round to the A-zone — third timed draw, same as Draw 1.

stages.name: Target Transition
stages.notes: Draw and fire 3 rounds to the body on the left target, transition, then fire 3 more to the body on the right target.

stages.name: One-Shot Draw 2
stages.notes: Draw and fire 1 round to the A-zone — second timed draw, same as Draw 1.

stages.name: One-Shot Draw 1
stages.notes: Draw and fire 1 round to the A-zone.

stages.name: Body to Head Transition
stages.notes: Draw and fire 3 rounds to the body, then 2 rounds to the head box.

stages.name: Slide-Lock Reload
stages.notes: Start with 3 rounds loaded. Fire 3 to the body, slide-lock reload, then fire 3 more to the body.

drills.name: 5-6-40 Drill
drills.notes: An ADAPTIV Defense Training carbine drill. Forty yards (or meters) onto a single target: six strings of five rounds each, thirty rounds in total, all fired from one full magazine. Each string is its own timed stage so every five rounds gets scored on its own, as a hit factor — points divided by time, with the USPSA A-zone scoring highest. The drill as published gives no par time, so none is set: work on shrinking the time without giving up points.

stages.name: String 2
stages.notes: Fire 5 more rounds into the same target — string 2 of 6, same magazine, no reload.

stages.name: String 3
stages.notes: Fire 5 more rounds into the same target — string 3 of 6, same magazine, no reload.

stages.name: String 6
stages.notes: Fire 5 more rounds into the same target — string 6 of 6, same magazine, no reload.

stages.name: String 1
stages.notes: Fire 5 rounds into the target.

stages.name: String 5
stages.notes: Fire 5 more rounds into the same target — string 5 of 6, same magazine, no reload.

stages.name: String 4
stages.notes: Fire 5 more rounds into the same target — string 4 of 6, same magazine, no reload.

drills.name: 5x5 Skills Test
drills.notes: 5 yards onto a 5-inch circle. Five strings of five rounds each, five seconds per string — draw, reload, strong hand only, weak hand only, and a turn-and-draw. All five rounds need to land inside the circle within par to clean a string. Bill Rogers' classic pistol skills benchmark; the exact task order varies by source, so treat this as one common version rather than the only correct one. The reload string starts on a deliberately short 2-round magazine, so the reload lands mid-string — reload with a full magazine to finish the other 3.

stages.name: String 3 — Strong Hand Only
stages.notes: From low ready, strong-hand only, fire 5 rounds.

stages.name: String 2 — Reload
stages.notes: From low ready with a 2-round magazine loaded, fire those 2, reload with a full magazine, then fire 3 more for 5 rounds total.

stages.name: String 5 — Turn and Draw
stages.notes: Start facing away from the target. Turn, draw, and fire 5 rounds.

stages.name: String 1 — Draw
stages.notes: Draw and fire 5 rounds into the circle.

stages.name: String 4 — Weak Hand Only
stages.notes: From low ready, support-hand only, fire 5 rounds.

drills.name: Air Marshal Qualification
drills.notes: 7 yards onto a QIT / FBI bottle target — 5 points for a hit inside the bottle, 2 points for an outer hit, 150 points available across the string. This is the classic TPC / old FAMS 30-round qualification; pass is 135/150 with no overtime shots on any stage. Shot cold, from concealment or low ready as each stage specifies. Six of the seven original strings are run twice back to back — each run is its own stage below, so hits get counted and the gun reset between them exactly as they would on the range. Two stages carry a reload: Stage 4 needs just 1 round loaded to reach it, Stage 7 needs 1 in the chamber with the magazine empty — load a fresh (or full) magazine for the reload itself on both.

stages.name: Stage 1 — Draw (Run 1)
stages.notes: From concealment, hands at sides. Draw and fire 1 round.

stages.name: Stage 4 — Reload (Run 1)
stages.notes: From low ready, fire 1, reload, fire 1. That's 1 round before the reload — load a magazine with just 1 in it, then reload with a fresh (or full) magazine for the second shot.

stages.name: Stage 7 — Slide Lock to Kneeling (Run 2)
stages.notes: Loaded with one in the chamber and an empty magazine — 1 round before the reload. From low ready, fire to slide lock, drop to a knee while reloading with a fresh (or full) magazine, fire one more — second identical run, same as Run 1.

stages.name: Stage 7 — Slide Lock to Kneeling (Run 1)
stages.notes: Loaded with one in the chamber and an empty magazine — 1 round before the reload. From low ready, fire to slide lock, drop to a knee while reloading with a fresh (or full) magazine, fire one more.

stages.name: Stage 2 — Double Tap (Run 1)
stages.notes: From low ready, a controlled pair.

stages.name: Stage 6 — 180° Pivot (Run 2)
stages.notes: Three targets 3 yd apart, starting turned away from concealment. Turn, draw, fire 1 on each target — same as Run 1, but pivot the opposite direction this time.

stages.name: Stage 1 — Draw (Run 2)
stages.notes: From concealment, hands at sides. Draw and fire 1 round — second identical run, same as Run 1.

stages.name: Stage 3 — Six Round String
stages.notes: From low ready, one continuous 6-round string. Run once.

stages.name: Stage 5 — Two Targets (Run 1)
stages.notes: Two targets 3 yd apart, from low ready. Fire 1 on each.

stages.name: Stage 6 — 180° Pivot (Run 1)
stages.notes: Three targets 3 yd apart, starting turned away from concealment. Turn, draw, fire 1 on each target.

stages.name: Stage 2 — Double Tap (Run 2)
stages.notes: From low ready, a controlled pair — second identical run, same as Run 1.

stages.name: Stage 4 — Reload (Run 2)
stages.notes: From low ready, fire 1, reload, fire 1 — second identical run, same as Run 1. Load a magazine with just 1 round again to start.

stages.name: Stage 5 — Two Targets (Run 2)
stages.notes: Two targets 3 yd apart, from low ready. Fire 1 on each — second identical run, same as Run 1.

drills.name: Bill Drill, Reload, Bill Drill
drills.notes: 7 yards onto an IPSC/USPSA target. Draw and fire a 6-round Bill Drill, reload, then fire a second 6-round Bill Drill — 12 rounds, one continuous string. Load a 6-round magazine (or top off to 6) so the reload lands right after the first Bill Drill, then reload with 6 or more for the second. Push pace without giving up the A-zone; the number to watch is how much time the reload adds over two clean Bill Drills.

stages.name: Bill Drill, Reload, Bill Drill
stages.notes: Draw and fire 6 rounds to the A-zone, reload, then fire 6 more to the A-zone. One continuous string. Load a 6-round magazine (or top off to 6) so the reload lands right after the first 6, then reload with 6 or more for the second.

drills.name: CQB Warm-Up
drills.notes: Two IPSC targets, rifle and pistol. A=5, C=3, D=1, miss=0, and any shot over the stage time standard counts as a miss. 240 points available — good is 216 (90%), pass is 204 (85%). Needs 36 rifle and 12 pistol rounds. The Rifle Reload stage starts with the rifle empty, so no rounds are needed going in — just have a full rifle magazine ready to reload with.

stages.name: Rifle Reload
stages.notes: At 7 yards, starting with an empty mag and bolt locked open, reload the rifle, then fire 3 rounds per target. No rounds needed before the reload — just have a full magazine ready.

stages.name: 40→20 yd Movement
stages.notes: Fire 2 rounds per target at 40 yards, move to 20, then fire 2 more per target at 20.

stages.name: 40 yd — Standing & Prone
stages.notes: Fire 2 rounds per target standing, then 2 rounds per target prone. Card lists 140 yd here but the setup says 40 yd — 40 assumed.

stages.name: 20→10 yd Movement
stages.notes: Fire 2 rounds per target at 20 yards, move to 10, then fire 2 more per target at 10.

stages.name: Rifle Empty Transition
stages.notes: At 7 yards, with the rifle mounted and empty, transition to pistol and fire 3 rounds per target.

stages.name: Rifle to Pistol Transition
stages.notes: At 10 yards, fire 3 rounds per target with the rifle, transition to pistol, then fire 3 more per target with the pistol.

drills.name: Carbine Failure Drill
drills.notes: Two identical strings at different distances — 7 and 15 yards — one IPSC/USPSA target. From low ready, fire 2 rounds to the body, assess, then 1 round to the head. Tests the body-to-head index shift under recoil as distance and apparent target size change.

stages.name: 15 Yards — 2 to Body, 1 to Head
stages.notes: From low ready, fire 2 rounds to the body, assess, then 1 round to the head — same sequence at the longer distance.

stages.name: 7 Yards — 2 to Body, 1 to Head
stages.notes: From low ready, fire 2 rounds to the body, assess, then 1 round to the head.

drills.name: Cold Heat
drills.notes: 7 yards onto a 6-inch circle, from concealment with your hands up in a fence or placating position and every holster retention device active. On the beep, draw and fire as many rounds as you can inside the 2-second par — shots after the 2-second par don't count at all, and going over par isn't a fail. Based on SLG's Cold Heat from pistol-training.com, which runs at 5 yards; this is set at 7. His benchmarks: one hit in 2 seconds is the minimum to carry in public, two hits is instructor level, three is top tier. Only the first "cold" run of a session counts for score; later runs are practice.

stages.name: Cold Heat
stages.notes: From concealment with your hands up, draw and fire as many rounds as you can into the 6-inch circle inside the 2-second par. Shots after the 2-second par don't count (going over par isn't a fail). 1 hit is the minimum, 2 is strong, 3 or more is top tier.

drills.name: Concealed Carry Humbler
drills.notes: 20 yards, IPSC target, from concealment under a cover garment. Three Bill Drills back to back with the times added together — 90 points available. Goal is a 10.0+ hit factor; a solid benchmark is clean runs of 3.0–3.5 seconds per Bill Drill.

stages.name: Bill Drill 3
stages.notes: Draw from concealment and fire 6 rounds to the A-zone — third identical run, same as Bill Drill 1.

stages.name: Bill Drill 1
stages.notes: Draw from concealment and fire 6 rounds to the A-zone.

stages.name: Bill Drill 2
stages.notes: Draw from concealment and fire 6 rounds to the A-zone — second identical run, same as Bill Drill 1.

drills.name: Dot Torture
drills.notes: 3 yards onto a Dot Torture target: ten 2-inch dots, worked in order, 50 rounds total. Not timed — every round either lands inside its dot or it doesn't, and the score is hits out of 50. David Blinder's drill, popularized by pistol-training.com. Clean it at 3 yards, then move back a yard and run it again. The last stage needs a reload between dots 9 and 10, so start each of its reps with just 1 round loaded.

stages.name: Dot 2 — Draw, 1 Round ×5
stages.notes: Draw and fire 1 round at dot 2. Holster. Do it 5 times.

stages.name: Dots 6–7 — Draw, 2 Each ×4
stages.notes: Draw, fire 2 rounds at dot 6 and 2 rounds at dot 7. Holster. Do it 4 times.

stages.name: Dot 1 — Slow Fire
stages.notes: Draw and fire 5 rounds at dot 1, slow fire.

stages.name: Dot 5 — Strong Hand Only
stages.notes: Fire 5 rounds at dot 5, strong hand only.

stages.name: Dots 9–10 — 1, Reload, 1 ×3
stages.notes: With 1 round loaded, draw and fire 1 round at dot 9, reload, fire 1 round at dot 10. Do it 3 times. That's 1 round before each reload — load a magazine with just 1 in it, then reload with a magazine holding at least 1 more.

stages.name: Dots 3–4 — Draw, 1 Each ×4
stages.notes: Draw, fire 1 round at dot 3 and 1 round at dot 4. Holster. Do it 4 times.

stages.name: Dot 8 — Support Hand Only
stages.notes: Fire 5 rounds at dot 8, support hand only.

drills.name: Dry Fire: Controlled Pairs
drills.notes: SAFETY: confirm the gun is completely unloaded and keep all ammunition out of the room before starting. Aim at a safe backstop, at a target about 7 yards away (or a printed target on the wall). On the start beep, draw and press twice before the par beep. A rep is clean only if the sights were settled on target for both presses. Let the sights return to the target and reset the trigger between the two presses. Reholster fully during the reset between reps.

stages.name: Pairs — 2.4 s
stages.notes: Comfortable par. Draw, settle, press, let the front sight settle, press again.

stages.name: Pairs — 1.7 s
stages.notes: Push par. Only call a rep clean if both presses had settled sights.

stages.name: Pairs — 2.0 s
stages.notes: Working par. Same cadence, no rushing the second press.

drills.name: Dry Fire: Draw to First Press
drills.notes: SAFETY: confirm the gun is completely unloaded and keep all ammunition out of the room before starting. Aim at a safe backstop, at a target about 7 yards away (or a printed target on the wall). On the start beep, draw and press once before the par beep. A rep is clean only if the sights were settled on target when the trigger broke. Reholster fully during the reset between reps.

stages.name: Draw — 2.0 s
stages.notes: Comfortable par. Smooth draw, settle the sights, press before the par beep.

stages.name: Draw — 1.2 s
stages.notes: Push par. Only call it clean if the sights were still settled.

stages.name: Draw — 1.5 s
stages.notes: Working par. Same draw, a little less hesitation.

drills.name: Dry Fire: One-Handed Draw
drills.notes: SAFETY: confirm the gun is completely unloaded and keep all ammunition out of the room before starting. Aim at a safe backstop, at a target about 7 yards away. Strong hand: draw with the strong hand only and press once, free hand to your chest. Support hand: start with the gun on target in both hands; on the beep, transfer to the support hand and press once. A rep is clean if the sights were settled when the trigger broke.

stages.name: Strong Hand Only — 2.5 s
stages.notes: Draw with the strong hand only and press once, free hand to your chest.

stages.name: Support Hand Only — 3.0 s
stages.notes: Start with the gun on target in both hands. On the beep, transfer to the support hand and press once.

drills.name: Dry Fire: Slide-Lock Reload
drills.notes: SAFETY: confirm the gun is completely unloaded and keep all live ammunition out of the room — use empty magazines or dummy rounds only. Start on target with the slide locked back or an empty magazine inserted, and a spare (empty or dummy-round) magazine on your belt. On the start beep, reload and press once before the par beep. A rep is clean if the magazine seated first time and the sights were settled at the press.

stages.name: Reload — 1.3 s
stages.notes: Reload, then press once. Push par.

stages.name: Reload — 2.0 s
stages.notes: Reload, then press once. Comfortable par.

stages.name: Reload — 1.6 s
stages.notes: Reload, then press once. Working par.

drills.name: Dry Fire: Target Transitions
drills.notes: SAFETY: confirm the gun is completely unloaded and keep all ammunition out of the room before starting. Set two or three targets (or printed targets on a safe wall) about a yard apart at 7 yards. Start at the low ready. On the start beep, press once on each target before the par beep. A rep is clean if the sights stopped on each target before each press, with no overswing.

stages.name: Two Targets — 1.5 s
stages.notes: From low ready, one press per target, left to right.

stages.name: Three Targets — 2.0 s
stages.notes: From low ready, one press per target, left to right.

drills.name: Dry Fire: Trigger Press Ladder
drills.notes: SAFETY: confirm the gun is completely unloaded and keep all ammunition out of the room before starting. Aim at a small spot on a safe wall about 5 yards away (or a printed target). Start with the gun on target and your finger on the trigger. On the start beep, press once before the par beep. A rep is clean if the sights did not move when the trigger broke — the same press every time, only faster.

stages.name: Medium — 1.0 s
stages.notes: Same press, less time. Keep the sights still.

stages.name: Slow — 2.0 s
stages.notes: Gun on target, finger on the trigger. One deliberate press.

stages.name: Fast — 0.5 s
stages.notes: Straight through the press. Only call clean presses clean.

drills.name: El Presidente
drills.notes: 10 yards, three IPSC/USPSA targets about a yard apart. Start with your back to the targets, hands relaxed at your sides. On the signal, turn 180°, draw, and fire 2 rounds on each target, reload, then fire 2 more rounds on each target — 12 rounds, one continuous string. Load a 6-round magazine (or top off to 6) so the reload lands right after the first pass, then reload with another 6 for the back half. Jeff Cooper's original drill; his "expert" standard was 10 seconds, and competitive shooters today run it well under 5.

stages.name: Turn, Draw, Reload
stages.notes: Start facing away from the targets. Turn, draw, 2 rounds on each of 3 targets — 6 rounds — reload, then 2 more rounds on each target for the final 6. One continuous string. Load a 6-round magazine (or top off to 6) so the reload lands right after the first pass.

drills.name: FAST Drill (Forty-Five And Ten)
drills.notes: 7 yards. Draw and fire 2 rounds to a 3×5 index card standing in for the head, reload, then fire 4 rounds to an 8-inch circle standing in for the body — six rounds, one continuous string. Load a 2-round magazine (or top off to 2) so the reload lands right after the head card, then reload with 4 or more for the body. Time and hits both count: a shot outside either zone fails the run no matter how fast it was. Reference tiers from the pistol-training.com community this drill comes from: sub-10s clean is a solid baseline, sub-7s is advanced, and sub-5s clean is the "Distinguished" tier serious shooters chase.

stages.name: Draw, 2 Head, Reload, 4 Body
stages.notes: Draw and fire 2 rounds to the head card, reload, then fire 4 rounds to the body circle. One continuous string. That's 2 rounds before the reload, so load a 2-round magazine (or top off to 2), then reload with 4 or more for the body.

drills.name: FBI Qualification
drills.notes: 50 rounds on a QIT-99 target. Every hit inside the bottle silhouette is worth 2 points, 100 points available across ten stages. All draws are from concealment unless a stage says otherwise. Agents pass at 80, instructors at 90. Where a stage calls for ready position, that means muzzle at 45° to the ground, finger off the trigger. The 7 Yards — Reload stage needs a 4-round magazine loaded to reach the reload, then a second 4-round (or full) magazine for the back half.

stages.name: 7 Yards — Ready
stages.notes: From low ready, fire 5 rounds.

stages.name: 15 Yards — Ready
stages.notes: From low ready, fire 3 rounds.

stages.name: 3 Yards — Strong/Support Hand
stages.notes: Draw and fire 3 rounds strong-hand only, switch hands, then fire 3 more support-hand only.

stages.name: 7 Yards — Draw
stages.notes: Draw and fire 5 rounds.

stages.name: 5 Yards — Draw
stages.notes: Draw and fire 3 rounds.

stages.name: 5 Yards — Ready, 3 Rounds
stages.notes: From low ready, fire 3 rounds.

stages.name: 25 Yards — Standing to Kneeling
stages.notes: Draw and fire 4 rounds standing, drop to kneeling, then fire 4 more.

stages.name: 7 Yards — Reload
stages.notes: From low ready, fire 4 rounds, execute an emergency reload, then fire 4 more. That's 4 rounds before the reload, so load a 4-round magazine (or top off to 4), then reload with another 4 (or full) for the back half.

stages.name: 5 Yards — Ready, 6 Rounds
stages.notes: From low ready, fire 6 rounds.

stages.name: 15 Yards — Draw
stages.notes: Draw and fire 3 rounds.

drills.name: First Shot — Steel
drills.notes: 7 yards onto a single steel target. Draw and fire one round on the beep — scored hit or miss, with the raw time to first shot as the number that matters. No par time; this is a baseline check, not a standard to pass.

stages.name: Draw — 1 Round
stages.notes: From holster or ready, on the beep.

drills.name: MXAD Drill
drills.notes: Matt Pranka / Tenicor. Close target at about 5 yards, far target at about 12 yards, from concealment or ready. Push an aggressive pace while staying relaxed and visually precise — the point is to train at the edge where mistakes happen so you learn to see and correct them.

stages.name: Close Bill Drill into Far Transition
stages.notes: Draw and fire 6 rounds on the 5 yd target, then immediately transition and fire 2 rounds on the 12 yd target. One continuous string, so it's a single stage.

drills.name: Man Card (Short Card)
drills.notes: 25 yards onto C-zone steel, or an IPSC target counting C-zone hits only. Shots must land in the C-zone — a miss or an overtime shot is a failure. Typically two attempts per stage. Needs a full pistol magazine, a full rifle magazine, and one empty rifle magazine for the transition stage.

stages.name: Pistol — From Holster
stages.notes: Draw from holster and fire 1 round.

stages.name: Pistol — Compressed Ready
stages.notes: From compressed ready, fire 1 round.

stages.name: Rifle — High Ready
stages.notes: From high ready, stock under the armpit, fire 1 round.

stages.name: Rifle to Pistol Transition
stages.notes: Fire 1 round rifle, transition to pistol, then fire 1 round pistol. Par covers the whole string.

stages.name: Rifle — Low Ready
stages.notes: From low ready — muzzle at 45° or similar, safety on, finger off the trigger — fire 1 round.

drills.name: Minimum Concealed Carry Standard
drills.notes: IPSC/USPSA target, every stage from low ready, run sequentially on the same target. The final stage is untimed.

stages.name: 7 yd — 6 Rounds Body
stages.notes: From low ready, fire 6 rounds to the body A-zone.

stages.name: 10 yd — 1 Shot Head
stages.notes: From low ready, fire 1 round to the head box. Untimed — accuracy only.

stages.name: 5 yd — 1 Shot Head
stages.notes: From low ready, fire 1 round to the head box.

stages.name: 3 yd — 4 Rounds Body
stages.notes: From low ready, fire 4 rounds to the body A-zone.

drills.name: Mozambique / Failure to Stop Drill
drills.notes: 7 yards onto an IPSC/USPSA target. Draw and fire 2 rounds to the body, assess, then fire 1 round to the head — three rounds, one continuous string. Named for an account from the Mozambican Civil War where two solid body hits failed to stop a threat, forcing a head shot; still one of the most commonly drilled failure responses. No official par — the point is a smooth, controlled follow-up onto the head after the body pair, not raw speed.

stages.name: 2 to Body, 1 to Head
stages.notes: Draw and fire 2 rounds to the body, assess, then 1 round to the head. One continuous string.

drills.name: PSTG Criss Cross Drill
drills.notes: 7 yards, three USPSA/IPSC targets about a yard apart: left, center, right. The full sequence runs twice with a reload in the middle and no stop, so it's timed as one 20-round string. Load a 10-round magazine (or top off to 10) for the first pass, then reload with another 10 for the second.

stages.name: Criss Cross — Full Sequence
stages.notes: Center body 2 → left head 2 → center 2 → right head 2 → center 2, reload, then repeat the identical sequence. That's 10 rounds before the reload, so load a 10-round magazine (or top off to 10) to reach it clean, then reload with another 10 for the second half.

drills.name: Pistol Bill Drill
drills.notes: 7 yards onto a single steel target. Draw and fire 6 rounds as fast as you can get hits — scored hit or miss per round, with time as the number that matters. No par time; push speed until misses show up, then back off half a step.

stages.name: Bill Drill
stages.notes: Draw from holster or ready, 6 rounds, one steel target.

drills.name: Pistol Bill Drill Rundown
drills.notes: 25, 10, and 5 yards, one IPSC/USPSA target, run as a single continuous 18-round string — draw, movement, an emergency reload on the move, and a final visual-confirmation string. Load a 12-round magazine (or top off to 12) to make it to the reload, then reload with 6 (or more) for the final string. Tests draw, movement, transitions, reload, and visual confirmation together. Push pace without giving up hits; a strong benchmark is roughly a 7.5+ hit factor.

stages.name: 25 → 10 → 5 Yards
stages.notes: Start holstered at 25 yards. Draw and fire 6, sprint to 10 yards and fire 6 more — 12 rounds — then move to 5 yards, performing a mandatory emergency reload on the move, and fire the final 6. One continuous string, so it's modelled as a single stage. Load a 12-round magazine (or top off to 12) to make it to the reload, then reload with 6 for the last string.

drills.name: Rifle 5x5 Standards
drills.notes: 25 yards, one IPSC/USPSA target, from low ready. Five separate 5-round strings, each timed on its own with a tighter par than the last — 6.0, 5.5, 5.0, 4.5, then 4.0 seconds. Clean hits inside the A-zone within par to pass a string; losing hits as the par shrinks is the expected trade-off that shows where your speed limit actually is.

stages.name: String 3 — 5.0s Par
stages.notes: From low ready, fire 5 rounds to the A-zone within par — third string, tighter par than String 2.

stages.name: String 1 — 6.0s Par
stages.notes: From low ready, fire 5 rounds to the A-zone within par.

stages.name: String 5 — 4.0s Par
stages.notes: From low ready, fire 5 rounds to the A-zone within par — fifth and final string, tightest par of the set.

stages.name: String 4 — 4.5s Par
stages.notes: From low ready, fire 5 rounds to the A-zone within par — fourth string, tighter par than String 3.

stages.name: String 2 — 5.5s Par
stages.notes: From low ready, fire 5 rounds to the A-zone within par — second string, tighter par than String 1.

drills.name: Rifle Bill Drill
drills.notes: 10 yards onto a single steel target. From low ready, fire 6 rounds as fast as you can keep them on steel — scored hit or miss per round, with time as the number that matters. No par time; push speed until misses show up, then back off half a step. Direct carbine analog of the Pistol Bill Drill.

stages.name: Rifle Bill Drill
stages.notes: From low ready, fire 6 rounds, one steel target.

drills.name: State Police Red Dot Qualification
drills.notes: Duty-style or EDC concealed holster. Hits must land in the designated body or head zone; each miss or out-of-zone shot adds one second. The standard is an aggregate: 15 seconds total across all five stages including penalties, so stages carry no individual par. Reference times in the stage notes are example clean performances, not requirements.

stages.name: 20 yd — 1 Shot Body
stages.notes: Draw from concealment and fire 1 round to the body. Reference 1.60–1.75s.

stages.name: 4 yd — 6 Body + 1 Head
stages.notes: From compressed ready, fire 6 rounds to the body and 1 round to the head. Reference 1.80–2.35s clean.

stages.name: 10 yd — 1 Shot Head
stages.notes: Draw and fire 1 round to the head box. Reference 1.55–1.82s clean.

stages.name: 10 yd — 6 Shots Body
stages.notes: Draw and fire 6 rounds to the body. Reference 3.10–3.40s clean.

stages.name: 12→5 yd — 5 Shots Body
stages.notes: From ready position, fire 5 rounds to the body while advancing from 12 to 5 yards. Reference 3.20–3.85s clean.

drills.name: The Test (Cold Start)
drills.notes: 25 yards onto a 3×5 index card. Shoot it cold, before any warm-up — that's the whole point of the drill.

stages.name: Rifle — 1 Round from Ready
stages.notes: From high or low ready, fire 1 round.

stages.name: Pistol — 1 Round from Holster
stages.notes: Draw from holster and fire 1 round.

drills.name: The Test (Cold Start) — Pistol Only
drills.notes: 25 yards onto a 3×5 index card. Shoot it cold, before any warm-up — that's the whole point of the drill. Same standard as the full Test, minus the rifle stage, for pistol-only range days.

stages.name: Pistol — 1 Round from Holster
stages.notes: Draw from holster and fire 1 round.

drills.name: Trigger Iso Drill
drills.notes: BAER Solutions. 2.5–3 yards onto four 1-inch pasters, one full magazine per paster. Not timed — this is a diagnostic. Press the trigger straight back without disturbing the sights, from the pad or distal joint rather than deep on the finger. Experiment with pressing toward your thumb (often pulls left for right-handers), wrist (straight back), or elbow (often corrects a left pull). Call every shot before you look at the target, then verify. If shots pull left, deliberately press the opposite way on the next shot to feel the difference. Round counts assume 15-round magazines — adjust to your pistol.

stages.name: Strong Hand Only
stages.notes: Fire the entire magazine at the first paster, strong-hand only.

stages.name: Strong Hand Only (again)
stages.notes: Fire the entire magazine at the third paster, strong-hand only again.

stages.name: Support Hand Only
stages.notes: Fire the entire magazine at the second paster, support-hand only.

stages.name: Both Hands
stages.notes: Fire the entire magazine at the fourth paster, using both hands.

drills.name: VTAC 1-5 Drill
drills.notes: Kyle Lamb / Viking Tactics. Five IPSC/USPSA targets in a row, about 1 yard apart, at 7 yards. One continuous 30-round string with no par time — push pace while keeping every round on target, then compare total time run to run. A strong carbine time is under 10 seconds.

stages.name: 1-5 Ascend/Descend
stages.notes: From low ready, fire 1 round on target 1, 2 on target 2, 3 on target 3, 4 on target 4, and 5 on target 5 — left to right. Then reverse: 5 rounds on target 5 back down to 1 round on target 1, right to left. One continuous string.
